parsed_response.reasoning: Verified against the diff: packages/types/Calendar.d.ts changes the interface to `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)`, yet the Lark (`async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)`), Office365 (`async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)`), and BaseCalendarService implementations are unchanged in this diff and still take one parameter — which TypeScript permits since fewer-parameter implementations satisfy the signature. The mechanism described (credential-based destination selection is only enforceable by the Google implementation; other implementations silently fall back to first-destination-calendar behavior, e.g. Lark's `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`) is accurate. This is a real, specific contract/architecture risk created by this change (future providers or edits compile cleanly while ignoring per-credential routing), not a demonstrable current defect, so it's a substantive advisory rather than a bug.

judged_text: The Calendar interface now mandates a credentialId routing parameter that TypeScript lets implementers silently ignore (fewer-parameter implementations are legal), and three of the four implementations in this diff (Lark, Office365, BaseCalendarService) do ignore it, so the boundary cannot enforce the per-credential destination selection it was added to guarantee. The next calendar provider — or any future edit to the non-Google implementations — compiles cleanly while creating events on the wrong calendar, which is the exact bug class shipped in this PR, because the contract's key parameter is unenforceable at the interface.
